A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same ARB-LLM paper, with matching sections, figures, tables and equations. Neither contains an appendix: both end with references and refer to separate supplementary files. Those external proofs and additional results are outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original ARB-LLM perplexity and zero-shot QA evaluations, component ablations, and timing and memory comparisons in Section 4, Tables 1–6 and Figures 1 and 6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports CSR-compressed bitmap memory estimates in Table 6.

M1.justification: ARB, ARB-X, ARB-RC and CGB retain the same objectives, parameter updates and partitioning procedures. The revised explanation after Equation 6 clarifies existing binary matrices and scaling/shifting factors; it does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same WikiText2, PTB and C4 language-modeling coverage and seven zero-shot QA datasets, using the same OPT, LLaMA and Vicuna families. No dataset, task or represented population is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including RTN, GPTQ, PB-LLM, BiLLM and full precision where originally included. Table 6 adds compressed-storage figures for existing rows, without adding a comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 extends memory accounting from the original values, now identified as raw-bitmap storage, to both raw and CSR-compressed bitmap storage. This adds a storage-accounting configuration; benchmark metrics, calibration sample counts, model sizes and iteration settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 extends the resource analysis to show how bitmap compression affects memory usage and the storage advantage over existing comparators. This is a limited additional analysis; the six component and sensitivity studies in Table 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The retained iteration-count ablation concerns algorithm iterations, not statistical replication.

E6.justification: Table 6 retains every original memory value and adds CSR estimates. For LLaMA-7B/13B, ARB-LLMRC with CGB adds 2.09/3.73 GB alongside the retained raw values of 2.83/5.17 GB; BiLLM adds 2.19/3.92 GB alongside 2.93/5.36 GB. These are additional storage-representation results, not same-setting performance gains. Perplexity, QA, ablation and timing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and Equations 1–14 are unchanged. The replacement explanation after Equation 6 restates the roles and dimensions of existing symbols without changing the mathematical procedure or claims. Neither PDF includes the separately referenced proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about alternating refinement, calibration-aware and row-column variants, CGB, superiority over binary PTQ baselines, and surpassing same-size FP16 models on zero-shot QA.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of distribution alignment and column-wise scaling, the optimization difficulty of incorporating calibration data into ARB-RC, and the storage trade-offs of CGB and additional groups. The revised memory paragraph describes the added reporting convention without introducing a new mechanism or applicability limitation.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies raw versus CSR-compressed bitmap accounting. Its abstract also replaces the future code-and-model release sentence with a Code link at the same address, although the reproducibility statement still promises a future release; actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Hardware and implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning against earlier binarization and quantization work are unchanged. Correcting ZerqQuant to ZeroQuant does not introduce a different cited work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to the abstract, Equation 6 explanation and memory paragraph, corrects the ZeroQuant spelling, and adds acknowledgments and publication-header text. The scientific section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 6 changes from single memory entries to paired raw/CSR entries and updates its caption to specify units and representations. Publication headers, local spacing and reference pagination also change. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by distinguishing raw and CSR-compressed storage and reporting both consistently for the existing quantized comparators in Table 6. The clearer Equation 6 explanation also modestly improves readability. These are useful but limited gains: the method and main empirical evidence are unchanged, and supplementary proofs and calculation details remain outside both supplied PDFs.
